title: Primary Three Christian Religious Education – Term III 2026
summary: NCDC order: Forgiveness and Acceptance (Weeks 1–3); Treating Others Fairly (Weeks 4–6); Jesus Brings Joy (Weeks 7–9); The Joy of Christmas (Week 10). Two 40-minute teaching periods per week. The third period is reserved by Ledgerly for weekly review.

units.title: Forgiveness and Acceptance
units.competences: Learners explain forgiveness, name traditional reconciliation practices, discuss peaceful conflict resolution, and show tolerance.

sources.quote: Talking about the importance of forgiveness
FORGIVENESS AND ACCEPTANCE

lessons.title: Meaning of forgiveness
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to explain the meaning of forgiveness and identify words used to seek forgiveness.

sources.quote: Talking about traditional ways of encouraging
Forgiveness means stopping being angry

lessons.title: Traditional ways of encouraging forgiveness
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to name traditional ways of encouraging forgiveness, including apologising and reconciliation.

sources.quote: Traditional ways of encouraging
Traditional ways of encouraging forgiveness

lessons.title: Reasons for forgiving others
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to state reasons why people need to forgive one another.

sources.quote: Talking about the importance of forgiveness
Reasons why we need to forgive

lessons.title: Resolving disagreements without violence
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to describe steps for resolving disagreements without violence.

sources.quote: Resolving differences without
Resolving misunderstanding without violence

lessons.title: Causes of conflict
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to identify differences and wrongdoings that may cause misunderstanding.

sources.quote: Identifying causes of conflicts
Causes of misunderstandings/violence

lessons.title: Accepting and tolerating other people
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to describe ways of accepting other people's differences peacefully.

sources.quote: Talking about ways of accepting and being tolerant
Ways of accepting and tolerating our differences

units.title: Treating Others Fairly
units.competences: Learners distinguish fair and unfair conduct, explain its effects, describe John the Baptist's teaching and identify ways to avoid cheating.

sources.quote: Treating Others Fairly
TREATING OTHERS FAIRLY

lessons.title: Fair and unfair behaviour
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to distinguish fair from unfair behaviour and give examples.

sources.quote: Fair and unfair behaviour
Being fair means treating each person equally.

lessons.title: Results of fair and unfair behaviour
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to give consequences of treating people fairly and unfairly.

sources.quote: Talking about the importance of fair
Results of fair behaviour.

lessons.title: Reasons people behave unfairly
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to identify reasons that can lead to unfair treatment.

sources.quote: Talking about the causes of unfair
Reasons why some people behave unfairly

lessons.title: John the Baptist's teaching about fairness
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to state the teaching about sharing and fair collection of taxes.

sources.quote: Talking about the need to treat others
How John the Baptist teaches us to be fair

lessons.title: Meaning and forms of cheating
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to explain cheating and identify dishonest practices.

sources.quote: Identifying causes of cheating
Forms of cheating

lessons.title: Why cheating is wrong and how to avoid it
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to explain reasons against cheating and ways to avoid it.

sources.quote: Talking about how to avoid cheating
Ways how you can avoid cheating

units.title: Jesus Brings Joy
units.competences: Learners relate Old Testament prophecies to Jesus' coming, tell the first Christmas story and describe Christmas preparations.

sources.quote: Jesus Brings Joy
JESUS BRINGS JOY

lessons.title: Old Testament prophecies of Jesus' coming
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to name prophets who foretold the coming of Jesus.

sources.quote: Naming different prophets in the Old Testament
Old prophesies about Jesus

lessons.title: How Jesus fulfilled the prophecies
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to relate the foretold birth of Jesus to Bethlehem and his family lineage.

sources.quote: Talking about the importance of the prophecy
That Jesus would be born in a small town called Bethlehem.

lessons.title: The birth of Jesus
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to describe the birth of Jesus and its significance for Christians.

sources.quote: Identifying the most important events of the first
Jesus was born on the first Christmas.

lessons.title: Angels and shepherds at the first Christmas
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to describe the shepherds' part in the Christmas story.

sources.quote: the visit of Angels to the
The shepherds were the first people to know about Jesus

lessons.title: Wise men and their gifts
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to name the gifts brought by the wise men to baby Jesus.

sources.quote: the visit of the wise men
The Magi gave baby Jesus these gifts;

lessons.title: Preparing for Christmas with others
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to identify ways people prepare for and share Christmas joy.

sources.quote: Talking about how to prepare for Christmas at home
Sending Christmas cards to friends and relatives.

units.title: The Joy of Christmas
units.competences: Learners describe Christmas cards, messages and carols and answer assessment questions drawn from the supplied materials.

sources.quote: Preparation for Christmas play
Preparation for Christmas

lessons.title: Making Christmas cards and messages
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to describe making a Christmas card and writing a greeting.

sources.quote: Designing Christmas cards
Writing Christmas messages

lessons.title: End-of-term assessment: Christmas preparations and celebrations
objectives: By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to answer sourced questions on Christmas preparations, celebration and carols.

sources.quote: Singing Christmas carols
On which day do Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus Christ?

gaps: The NCDC Theme 'The Joy of Christmas' extends to Weeks 10–12; this school's ten-week term permits only the first week of the theme. Remaining Christmas-play activities require further pacing or review allocation.
The last lesson is reserved for an end-of-term assessment using source questions. The full assessment paper and answer key must be selected from the pack when the lesson is written.
